chunks: Irshad al-Mufid: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from a number of his men, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:

I was at the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when a man from the people of Sham came … then he [the Imam] said: O Hisham, you never fall flat [settle on the ground], every time it seems that you are about to come to ground [i.e. be defeated] you just bend your legs [to able to leap] and off you fly away again. The likes of you should debate the people. Therefore be wary of slipping and you will find that succor is around the corner if Allah wills.

key_terms.تَلْوِي رِجْلَيْكَ: you bend your legs (idiom for agility/preparing to leap)
key_terms.هشام: Hisham (ibn al-Hakam, a prominent companion and theologian)

ai.seo_question: What advice did Imam al-Sadiq give to Hisham ibn al-Hakam regarding public debate?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Mufid's *Irsad* highlights Hisham ibn al-Hakam’s renowned dialectical prowess, using the metaphor of a swift leap to illustrate his intellectual agility during theological debates. The Imam warns that such rapid-fire argumentation carries the risk of subtle errors (*zalah*), emphasizing the need for precision and mindfulness to ensure his intercession (*shafa'ah*) remains effective and divinely sanctioned.
